concept: Find items that appear together more often than chance would suggest.
use: Walmart mines baskets for complementary product pairs and uses the relationships in recommendations.
adv: Readable rules can support cross-selling without labeled outcomes.
lim: Popularity and promotions distort co-occurrence. A relationship does not prove causation.
take: Products bought together can inform products recommended together.
detail: Walmart evaluated FP-Growth, then selected simpler pairwise co-occurrence rules for scale.
notes: Association rules describe conditional co-occurrence. Support = P(A and B). Confidence = P(B given A). Lift = P(B given A) / P(B). Lift above 1 indicates positive association against independence. Apriori and FP-Growth are common frequent-itemset algorithms. Walmart evaluated distributed FP-Growth but selected a pairwise probability approach. No revenue uplift is claimed here. Evaluation: minimum support, lift and an online recommendation experiment.

concept: Assign one of two labels, often by applying a threshold to a risk score.
use: Infobip Signals distinguishes legitimate SMS from bot traffic and blocks fraudulent requests for Cabify.
adv: Automates high-volume decisions and reduces manual intervention.
lim: False positives can block real customers. Attack patterns change over time.
take: A two-way prediction becomes useful when its errors have clear business costs.
detail: Infobip reports 15.7% less AIT-related financial loss in one quarter. Model architecture is undisclosed.
source: Infobip customer case with Cabify testimony
notes: Binary classification is the task abstraction: legitimate versus bot-generated traffic. The supplier describes an ML system that combines patterns and anomaly signals. It does not disclose a specific supervised classifier, training labels or threshold. AIT means Artificial Inflation of Traffic. The 15.7% figure describes financial loss over one quarter after fraud/authentication changes. It is a supplier-reported business result, not classification accuracy or an isolated model effect. Generic evaluation: precision, recall, PR-AUC and cost at the operating threshold.

status: COTA support assistant in production (2018 account)
concept: Choose one category from three or more mutually exclusive alternatives.
use: Uber COTA predicts support issue types from ticket text and trip context, helping agents select the right category.
adv: Reduces the effort of navigating a large support taxonomy.
lim: Similar issues and rare categories can confuse the classifier.
take: A ticket gets one issue category, with a human confirming the model’s suggestions.
detail: Issue identification is separate from COTA’s solution-ranking task.
notes: This case isolates issue-type identification. The 2018 account describes a random-forest baseline and a later neural alternative. COTA presents three likely issue types for human selection. Its separate solution ranker scores ticket-solution pairs with binary random forests. Do not treat those ranked solutions as simultaneous class labels. The source describes historical deployment. Evaluate macro-F1, rare-class recall and top-k accuracy.

concept: Assign zero, one or several labels to the same observation.
use: Amazon predicts customer action propensities across thousands of product categories, allowing overlapping interests.
adv: Represents overlapping interests without forcing a single segment.
lim: Rare labels and different thresholds make training and evaluation harder.
take: The same customer can belong to several useful categories at once.
detail: Amazon describes MXNet models with Spark and Deep Java Library inference.
notes: We interpret the requested “multicategoría” as multilabel classification, the standard English term for non-exclusive labels. Binary relevance is a common baseline that trains one binary model per label. Neural models can share a representation across labels. Amazon documents a multilabel customer action propensity task; this does not mean one hard label for every category. Evaluate per-label precision/recall, micro-F1 and precision at k. Independent thresholds need calibration.

concept: Discover groups with similar behavior without predefined group labels.
use: Spotify combines UMAP with recursive HDBSCAN to discover finer segments of users.
adv: Finds unexpected segments and supports targeted user research.
lim: Feature choices shape the groups. Stable clusters still need human validation.
take: Clustering discovers groups that researchers can then investigate.
detail: Spotify uses XGBoost and SHAP to explain the resulting segments.
notes: UMAP compresses high-dimensional data. HDBSCAN discovers dense groups and can leave some observations as noise. Recursion means repeating that process within a group. Spotify then learns one-versus-all XGBoost models and uses SHAP to understand the features associated with each cluster. This source describes user segmentation and research. It does not establish that Discover Weekly uses this pipeline. Evaluate stability across samples and feature choices, then validate usefulness with researchers.

concept: Flag observations that differ from the expected pattern for their context.
use: Adyen models merchant payment volumes and alerts teams when observations fall outside expected bounds.
adv: Can identify rare operational problems without labeled incident examples.
lim: Holidays and merchant changes cause false alerts. Sensitive thresholds increase noise.
take: An anomaly is unusual relative to a meaningful baseline.
detail: The model captures trend, seasonality and events, with quantile regression for uncertainty bounds.
notes: This is a contextual time-series anomaly detector. A sudden drop at a normally busy time is more informative than a low volume at night. Adyen models trend, seasonality and events, and uses quadratic quantile regression on residuals for bounds. The company evaluated and rejected isolation forests and autoencoders for this application, so those are not the deployed methods here. Evaluate incident detection rate, false alerts and time to detection. An alert requires investigation rather than establishing a root cause.

date: Product page and 17 Feb 2021 engineering post
concept: Estimate a continuous number from explanatory features.
use: idealista/data combines comparables and hedonic ML to estimate property values from location and attributes.
adv: Produces consistent estimates across large property portfolios.
lim: Missing attributes and market changes reduce accuracy. Estimates differ from completed sale prices.
take: Regression estimates a number from the characteristics of an observation.
detail: The company discloses the valuation approach, but not the exact estimator.
notes: A hedonic model relates property value to attributes such as location, size and property type. A linear regressor is an interpretable teaching baseline; the company does not say that its production estimator is linear regression. Automated valuation combines ML with comparable properties. A model estimate is not a guaranteed sale price or a formal appraisal. Evaluate MAE in euros and percentage errors, segmented by location and property type. Prediction alone does not identify causal price drivers.

concept: Estimate future values using time-dependent patterns and available drivers.
use: MeteoFlow combines weather and generation data, using ML to refine renewable output forecasts.
adv: Supports planning when wind and solar output vary with weather.
lim: Forecast uncertainty grows with the horizon and unexpected weather changes.
take: Forecasting turns an uncertain future into a quantified planning input.
detail: Iberdrola documents 450+ wind and solar plants, with hourly forecasts up to 96 hours.
notes: Regression predicts a numeric target. Forecasting adds a future horizon and temporal dependence, and can itself use regression. MeteoFlow also supplies daily forecasts up to ten days. Coverage and forecast horizons are deployment figures, not accuracy improvements. Iberdrola does not disclose the exact ML algorithm. Use rolling-origin backtesting, compare against a seasonal or persistence baseline, and measure interval coverage as well as MAE. A random train/test split can leak future information.

concept: Extract opinions from language and link each opinion to what it describes.
use: Booking.com links review opinions to 50+ aspects, such as cleanliness or location.
adv: Makes specific praise and complaints visible across many reviews.
lim: Sarcasm, mixed opinions and language differences can change interpretation.
take: A review can praise the location while criticizing the room.
detail: Aspect extraction identifies the subject. Sentiment analysis estimates the opinion about it.
source: Booking.com team / AWS Machine Learning Blog
notes: NLP is the broader field of computational language processing. Sentiment analysis is one task within it. Aspect-based analysis separates a whole-review score into opinions about specific aspects. “Great location, noisy room” is an illustrative sentence, not an actual Booking.com review. The source documents a data-labeling and training workflow using SageMaker Ground Truth. It does not publish a causal booking uplift from this system. Evaluate aspect extraction and sentiment separately, including language-specific error analysis.

concept: Extract structured facts and recurring signals from a large text collection.
use: ING’s Early Warning System combines signals from news and market data for credit-risk analysts.
adv: Helps analysts monitor more external information than they can read manually.
lim: Irrelevant or duplicated news creates noise. A signal still needs an analyst’s judgment.
take: Text mining turns a document stream into evidence for investigation.
detail: ING describes processing up to 80,000 news articles per day.
notes: Text mining focuses here on extracting and aggregating information from a corpus. It can use NLP components such as entity extraction, translation and sentiment. The distinction from the previous slide is the business output: company risk signals across many articles rather than the polarity of a review aspect. ING combines news processing with Refinitiv market data and analyst-defined alert criteria. The source treats stronger prediction capabilities as future ambition, so this slide makes no claim that the system predicts defaults. Evaluate relevance, entity-linking accuracy and analyst acceptance of alerts.

concept: Learn visual features that identify an object or a recurring configuration.
use: At Dingolfing, BMW compares a vehicle’s model badge with its order specification and flags missing or incorrect badges.
adv: Performs repeated visual checks at production speed.
lim: New components and lighting conditions require representative images and monitoring.
take: A learned visual pattern can turn a camera image into a quality check.
detail: Employees label component images and train a neural network.
notes: Pattern recognition spans many modalities and is broader than deep learning. This case specifically uses a trained neural network for visual recognition. A typical vision network learns features from pixels before predicting the component identity. The software then compares that identity to an order specification. BMW explicitly documents production use. We do not repeat the source’s “100% reliability” phrase as a general benchmark. Evaluate defect recall and false-rejection rate under actual factory conditions.

concept: Generate new images using learned visual structure.
use: Mango created Sunset Dream using real garment photos, a generative model and human selection and retouching.
adv: Expands creative options and supports repeatable production workflows.
lim: Product fidelity and editorial quality still require human art direction.
take: Generate new imagery while preserving the real product’s characteristics.
detail: Mango names no specific model architecture. Diffusion and GANs are general examples, not confirmed choices.
notes: Deep learning is the underlying technology family. Image generation is already generative AI, so it bridges the two sections. Diffusion models learn to reverse a noise process. GANs train a generator against a discriminator. These definitions illustrate algorithm families and are not claims about Mango’s implementation. The published campaign used real product photos and human editing. No time, cost or conversion improvement is claimed. Review garment fidelity, visible artifacts, usage rights and editorial suitability.

status: EKA live at Allianz Leben from July 2024
concept: Retrieve relevant knowledge before an LLM generates an answer.
use: Allianz EKA searches AWISO, summarizes relevant knowledge and links call-center staff to full sources.
adv: Makes internal knowledge easier to access and inspect.
lim: Missing retrieval results and outdated documents can still produce wrong answers.
take: Retrieve the evidence first, then generate a grounded answer.
detail: Allianz reports over 90% accuracy on common queries, without publishing the benchmark methodology.
notes: RAG means retrieval-augmented generation. It is a system architecture, not one algorithm or a guarantee of factual accuracy. EKA also includes fine-tuning and multi-agent elements; this slide isolates its documented RAG role. The source says the pilot began in July 2023 and went live at Allianz Leben one year later. The reported accuracy applies to common queries; it is not a universal correctness score. Evaluate retrieval recall, groundedness and end-to-end task correctness. Source links support verification.

concept: Generate related content across modalities, such as video and sound.
use: Google Vids uses Veo 3 to turn a text prompt into a video clip with sound, ready to preview and insert.
adv: Creates an audiovisual draft without filming or recording a first version.
lim: Visual continuity, speech and factual details still need human review.
take: One prompt can generate both the moving scene and its accompanying sound.
detail: The launch release documents 8-second clips. This is a shipped product capability.
notes: Modality means a form of information, such as text, image, audio or video. This product generates video and sound with Veo 3. The June 2025 launch account specifies 8-second clips and a prompt, preview, insert workflow. Users can mute audio after insertion. Training and product-demo prompts in the source are illustrative examples, not named customer deployments. This case concerns Google’s released product, rather than a claim about its internal marketing. Evaluate audiovisual consistency and accuracy against the brief.

status: Blue assistant deployed in Spain in 2025
concept: Coordinate specialized agents and tools to complete a bounded task.
use: Blue routes requests to a banking tool, an information agent or a clarification step.
adv: Connects conversational requests to defined account and card operations.
lim: Routing errors can select the wrong workflow. Permissions and confirmations matter.
take: Agents become operationally useful when the right tool can carry out the task.
detail: BBVA describes filtering 150+ operations to around 5–6 candidates before routing.
source: BBVA AI Factory and BBVA rollout announcement
notes: An agent combines model-based decisions with tools and state. Orchestration coordinates those parts, including specialization and handoffs. Blue represents banking operations as callable tools and loads a shortlist of descriptions for routing. The technical article describes multiple agent roles, not merely a scripted chatbot. The rollout announcement scheduled availability in Spain from 20 February 2025. Evaluate successful completion, wrong-tool rate, unauthorized actions and escalation quality. The numbered workflow on the preceding slide is a teaching abstraction, not a literal architecture diagram.
